q: The quantum threshold theorem for fault-tolerant quantum computation states that if physical error rates are below a threshold p_th, then:
opts: Arbitrarily long quantum computations can be performed reliably by concatenating error-correcting codes with overhead poly(log n)
The computation must use O(n²) qubits
exp: Quantum threshold theorem: if per-gate error rate p < p_th (≈ 10⁻²–10⁻⁴ for various schemes), concatenating CSS or surface codes gives error rates that drop doubly exponentially with code distance, enabling scalable quantum computation.
